steps.intent: Our objective is to renew the targeted Al-Shabaab sanctions regime for a further year, strengthen implementation against weapons flows from Yemen and maritime trafficking, and support Somali arms management, while preserving humanitarian exemptions. We expect difficulty from some members on the enhanced Panel of Experts mandate regarding Houthi links and on language reaffirming Somalia’s sovereignty and host-state consent, which may be sensitive for Ethiopia’s partners. We also anticipate scrutiny of the arms-related provisions to ensure they do not impede legitimate support to the Federal Government of Somalia.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports renewing the Somalia sanctions regime and thanks the United Kingdom for the balanced text. As an A3+ member, we ask that the text anchor AUSSOM and all international support in Somalia's sovereignty and consent, and that OP8 explicitly guard against actions undermining Somalia's unity and territorial integrity. We also suggest framing OP5 with international support so that it does not appear to penalize the Federal Government of Somalia.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime, the Panel of Experts mandate and the humanitarian exemption, and appreciates the UK's penholdership. We request minor clarifications to ensure full respect for coastal State sovereignty and UNCLOS in maritime inspections, and to keep the Panel's work on alleged Al-Shabaab-Houthi links within existing mandates and based on credible evidence. With these adjustments, China can support the text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime and the humanitarian exemption. We would like the text to include a clear operational call for unimpeded humanitarian access and compliance with international humanitarian and human rights law, and to make AUSSOM reporting cover IHL and human rights violations, including conflict-related sexual violence. These changes would strengthen the resolution’s protection focus without weakening its sanctions measures.
messages.France: France supports the UK’s draft as a good basis and welcomes its focus on AUSSOM, humanitarian exemptions and the Houthi arms-flow risk. We ask that OP4 expressly anchor maritime inspection and information-sharing in UNCLOS, and that OP6 capture financial and logistical links with Houthi actors and call for full Member State cooperation with the Panel. With these adjustments, France is ready to support the text.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate and thanks the United Kingdom for the balanced text. We request limited strengthening on maritime arms flows through the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, on coordination with relevant maritime security operations, and on respect for Somalia's sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with international law, including UNCLOS. These points reflect Greece's strong interest in maritime security and the rules-based order and would allow us to support the text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal and welcomes the penholder's text. As part of the A3+ and consistent with our previous statement on resolution 2776 (2025), we ask for a comprehensive assessment of the Al-Shabaab sanctions regime and for stronger language on Somalia's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We also suggest a small addition to OP5 to encourage capacity-building support for Somali arms and ammunition management.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate. We ask the penholder to reflect the need for sustainable and predictable funding for AUSSOM, and to strengthen OP8 so that all States refrain from unilateral agreements or actions undermining Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence. We can support OP10 with an explicit reference to fair and clear procedures.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime and the Panel's mandate, and welcomes the focus on maritime arms flows. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP4 with an explicit UNCLOS and flag-State reference, and to add human rights and gender reporting to the Panel's mandate. These changes would reinforce the rule of law and accountability without weakening the sanctions.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of the Somalia sanctions measures and the Panel of Experts mandate, and welcomes the UK’s balanced text, including its humanitarian exemption and focus on maritime arms flows. We request targeted technical improvements on predictable Panel reporting and on coordination with maritime security mechanisms, given the threat posed by weapons flows from Yemen and through maritime routes. We also propose a capacity-building paragraph to help Somalia and regional States strengthen arms management and border and maritime security, in full respect of Somali sovereignty.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports renewing the Somalia sanctions regime, but the text must reflect the Council’s earlier understanding that the regime is overdue for review and that the arms embargo should not hamper the Federal Government’s ability to ensure security. We therefore ask for an explicit safeguard that the embargo applies only to Al-Shabaab, IS-Somalia and designated entities, and for a review clause by mid-2026 with a view to easing or lifting the measures. We also suggest that OP6 be made evidence-based and avoid prejudging responsibility in the Yemen-related reporting.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of the sanctions regime and the humanitarian exemption, and is prepared to vote in favour. We ask the penholder to add a preambular reference to the African Union's central role and predictable financing for AU-led peace support operations, consistent with resolution 2719 (2023), and to strengthen OP8 on Somalia's sovereignty and territorial integrity, including against unilateral acts that undermine them. We also suggest minor coordination language in OP9 to reflect African ownership.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime and welcomes the explicit humanitarian exemption. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP3 against over-compliance and to make OP7 explicitly call for safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We also suggest the Panel assess the humanitarian impact of the measures in its reporting.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports renewal of the sanctions regime to combat Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia, but the text must not leave ambiguity about the arms embargo or external interference. We ask the penholder to make clear that the embargo targets designated terrorist entities only and does not impede support to the Federal Government of Somalia and AUSSOM, and to strengthen OP8 against agreements or actions affecting Somalia's territory without its consent. With these changes, we can support the draft.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports renewing the Somalia sanctions regime and welcomes the United Kingdom's penholder role, including the reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption in resolution 2664 (2022). We would like OP6 strengthened to reflect actual Houthi-Al-Shabaab links, including financing and weapons smuggling, and to have the Panel recommend designation targets. We also ask that OP10 make clear the Committee should prioritize designations, including for Houthi-Al-Shabaab cooperation. With those changes, we can support the text.

replies.Denmark: accepted: AUSSOM reporting now covers IHL and human rights including conflict-related sexual violence, and a protection and humanitarian-access paragraph is added.
replies.France: accepted: OP4 includes UNCLOS and information-sharing, while OP6 covers financial and logistical links and Member State cooperation.
replies.Greece: accepted: Red Sea and Gulf of Aden maritime flows, relevant maritime security operations, UNCLOS, and illicit maritime transfers are reflected.
replies.Guyana: accepted: OP5 capacity-building, strengthened OP8 territorial language, and a sanctions-regime assessment paragraph are included.
replies.Pakistan: accepted: AUSSOM funding language is added, OP8 covers land sea airspace and unilateral agreements, and OP10 includes fair and clear procedures.
replies.Panama: accepted: OP4 includes flag-State rights, OP2 adds IHL and gender reporting, and OP8 is broadened to all States while focusing on the region.
replies.Republic of Korea: accepted: Predictable written Panel updates, IMO and regional maritime coordination, and a capacity-building paragraph are added.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: OP1 clarifies designated targets and FGS exemptions and a review clause is added, but Houthi reference is retained with evidence and non-prejudgment caveats.
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: AU role and financing language is added, OP8 is strengthened, and AUSSOM coordination is reflected in OP11.
replies.Slovenia: accepted: OP3 addresses over-compliance, OP2 includes humanitarian-impact reporting, and OP7 calls for unhindered humanitarian access.
replies.Somalia: accepted: Red lines are addressed through explicit FGS and AUSSOM exemptions, targeted designations, strengthened territorial-integrity language, and consent and ownership provisions.
replies.United States of America: accepted: OP6 strengthens Houthi-Al-Shabaab links and designation recommendations, and OP10 prioritizes designations including Houthi-Al-Shabaab cooperation.

steps.summary: The revision preserves the core sanctions renewal and humanitarian exemption while incorporating broad A3-plus and host-State concerns on sovereignty, consent, and targeted measures. It retains and strengthens maritime and Houthi reporting and designation priorities for the United States and France, and adds review and assessment clauses and evidence safeguards to accommodate Russia and China. The text is expected to command consensus support.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the revised draft and welcomes the incorporation of our previous requests on sovereignty, territorial integrity and AUSSOM consent. We would like the preambular reference to AUSSOM funding to be translated into an operative request, consistent with resolution 2719 (2023), so that the Council supports predictable and sustainable financing for the mission. With that addition, we are ready to join consensus.
messages.China: China supports the revised text and will vote in favour. We appreciate the penholder’s constructive incorporation of our concerns regarding UNCLOS and coastal-State jurisdiction, credible evidence, and respect for existing mandates. The text appropriately reaffirms Somalia’s sovereignty and the Federal Government’s ownership, supports AUSSOM and African Union-led peace support operations, and maintains targeted sanctions with a humanitarian exemption. China encourages continued attention to Somali capacity-building and the timely review of sanctions measures.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the current revision and thanks the penholder for incorporating our prior requests on AUSSOM reporting and protection/humanitarian access. The text strikes an appropriate balance between targeted sanctions, the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022), respect for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and support for AUSSOM. Denmark is ready to vote in favour.
messages.France: France thanks the United Kingdom for incorporating our earlier requests; the text now properly reflects the maritime and Houthi-Al-Shabaab dimensions. France can support the draft, but we ask for one important adjustment to OP14 so that any easing is conditioned on concrete progress by the Federal Government of Somalia in arms and ammunition management and does not weaken the core arms embargo on Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia. With that clarification, France is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the current text and welcomes the inclusion of Red Sea and Gulf of Aden maritime flows, UNCLOS, relevant maritime security operations, and AUSSOM reporting on illicit maritime transfers. The text strikes a balanced approach between countering Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia, respecting Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and preserving humanitarian access. Greece will vote in favour and encourages full implementation of the sanctions and reporting provisions.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised text. Our key priorities—capacity-building support for Somalia, strengthened language on Somalia's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and a comprehensive assessment of the Al-Shabaab sanctions regime—are reflected in the draft. We also welcome the humanitarian safeguards and the provisions affirming Somali ownership of AUSSOM, and we are ready to join consensus.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier concerns on AUSSOM funding, Somali sovereignty and the fair and clear procedures of the sanctions Committee. We support the current text and will vote in favour. We encourage the Council to preserve unity and to keep the sanctions targeted, with full protection for humanitarian access.
messages.Panama: Panama welcomes the incorporation of its amendments on UNCLOS and flag-State rights, IHL and gender reporting, and the region-wide sovereignty language. The text strikes a balanced approach by renewing sanctions and supporting AUSSOM while preserving humanitarian access and respecting Somali sovereignty. Panama supports the draft as it stands and encourages the Council to adopt it.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea welcomes revision 1, which incorporates our earlier proposals on predictable Panel reporting, maritime coordination, and capacity-building. We support the balanced renewal of the Somalia sanctions regime, including the strengthened humanitarian exemption, maritime-security provisions, and the focus on preventing arms diversion. We encourage the Council to adopt the text promptly and by consensus.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation welcomes the incorporation of its key concerns regarding the Federal Government of Somalia's arms transfers and the review of the sanctions regime. We remain concerned that OP13 still prejudges the existence of Houthi-Al-Shabaab cooperation and could be used to expand the Somalia sanctions regime. We propose aligning OP13 with the caveats already agreed in OP6 by referring to credible evidence and relevant armed actors in Yemen without prejudging responsibility. With that adjustment, we are ready to support the text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft. We welcome the inclusion of the African Union’s central role and flexible financing language, the strengthened sovereignty provisions, and the AUSSOM coordination in OP11. We encourage Council unity in adopting the text.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the penholder for revision 1 and welcomes the inclusion of our earlier requests on humanitarian access, over-compliance, and humanitarian-impact reporting. We can support the text as it stands and encourage the Council to adopt it unanimously. We underline that implementation by AUSSOM and all parties must remain fully consistent with international law, including international humanitarian law and human rights law.
messages.Somalia: Somalia welcomes the revised draft, which now addresses our red lines on the FGS and AUSSOM exemption, territorial integrity, and AUSSOM consent and ownership. We support the text as it stands and call for its swift adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the current text. We appreciate the penholder’s incorporation of our earlier requests, particularly on strengthening reporting of Houthi–Al-Shabaab links and prioritizing designations, including for those involved in such cooperation. The draft maintains robust sanctions and arms-embargo measures while preserving humanitarian exemptions, and we call for full implementation and vigilant monitoring of maritime and arms flows. We will vote in favour.

The core Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia arms embargo, targeted sanctions, maritime provisions, and humanitarian exemption are preserved, and consensus is expected.

the notification and inspection measures applicable to the Federal Government of Somalia
where conditions permit,
on the basis of progress in arms and ammunition management and compliance with the notification procedures, while maintaining the arms embargo on Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia,
and to report to the Council;
Requests the Committee, with the support of the Panel of Experts and … by 15 July 2026 with recommendations on adjusting the regime as necessary;
Requests the Secretary-General to ensure that the United Nations provides appropriate support … access and on the impact of the measures on women and children;
Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria supported the draft after its priority request on AUSSOM funding was accepted, and the text aligns with its positions on Somali sovereignty, African-led peace support financing and targeted sanctions with humanitarian safeguards. It speaks in favour to reinforce those points before adoption.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported Somalia-related sanctions renewals and this draft aligns with its emphasis on Somali sovereignty, African Union-led security, targeted sanctions and humanitarian exemptions. No provisions cross China’s established red lines, so it votes in favour.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark’s established policy supports renewing Somalia sanctions and the Panel of Experts while safeguarding humanitarian access and AUSSOM’s Somali-owned mandate; the draft aligns with prior Danish votes and no changes were requested in negotiations. Voting in favour is consistent with Denmark’s multilateral and human-rights priorities.
reasons.France: France’s core priorities—targeted Al-Shabaab/IS-Somalia sanctions, countering Yemen arms flows, humanitarian safeguards, Somali sovereignty, AUSSOM support, and the accepted OP15 compromise—are reflected in the draft.
reasons.Greece: Greece has consistently supported previous renewals of the Somalia sanctions regime, and this draft reflects its priorities on sovereignty, humanitarian exemptions, international law including UNCLOS, and maritime security. No veto concerns arise, and Greece had already signalled support without requesting changes.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana consistently supports consensus renewals of Somalia sanctions and AUSSOM-related measures, and the draft reflects its priorities on sovereignty, humanitarian exemptions, and African-led peace support. No red lines were raised in negotiations, so Guyana votes in favour and explains its support before the vote.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan supported the draft in the last negotiation round and its key priorities—Somali sovereignty, counter-terrorism, and sustainable AU mission funding—are adequately reflected. No pre-vote explanation is necessary.
reasons.Panama: Panama has consistently supported multilateral counter-terrorism and sovereignty-preserving measures in Somalia and had already indicated support in the last negotiation round without requesting changes. The draft includes humanitarian safeguards and reaffirms Somali sovereignty, aligning with Panama’s foreign policy priorities.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported Security Council resolutions renewing Somalia sanctions and the Panel of Experts, and it participated constructively in this negotiation with no requested changes.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation has consistently supported targeted Al-Shabaab sanctions renewals, and the penholder accepted its important requested change on Yemen-related language. Moscow can therefore vote in favour while restating its standard concerns on sovereignty, humanitarian exemptions and predictable AUSSOM funding.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported Somalia-related Council resolutions and the UK penholder’s text, which aligns with its priorities on African-led peace operations, sovereignty, counterterrorism and humanitarian access. No changes were requested, so it votes in favour and explains its support.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has supported prior consensus Somalia sanctions resolutions and this draft reflects its priorities on humanitarian exemptions, IHL/HR, WPS, and Somali sovereignty. There is no basis to abstain or oppose.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft because it advances Somali sovereignty and territorial integrity, renews counter-terrorism sanctions, safeguards humanitarian access, and reinforces AUSSOM’s consent-based mandate and funding needs. Speaking before the vote allows Somalia to underscore these priorities, especially opposition to unilateral arrangements affecting its territory.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK is the penholder and strong supporter of the Somalia sanctions regime, AUSSOM, and Somali territorial integrity; voting yes advances its stated policy and the draft already reflects compromises. It will speak before the vote to signal support and encourage unanimous adoption.
reasons.United States of America: The United States supported the draft in the last negotiation round and its provisions align with established U.S. policy: renewing targeted Al-Shabaab/IS-Somalia sanctions, supporting AUSSOM, addressing Houthi-Al-Shabaab maritime and weapons links, and preserving humanitarian safeguards. No U.S. request was outstanding, so Washington would vote in favour.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholder for having taken on board our important request on predictable and sustainable funding for AUSSOM, consistent with resolution 2719 (2023), and for preserving the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022). Algeria supports the renewal of targeted measures against Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, while stressing that all sanctions must be implemented with full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Somalia, and that AUSSOM must operate with the consent and ownership of the Federal Government of Somalia. We also call on all States in the region to refrain from unilateral arrangements affecting Somali territory without the consent of the Federal Government and to resolve disputes through peaceful dialogue.
before.China: China will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, and we welcome the continued role of the African Union, including AUSSOM, in supporting Somalia’s peace and security. China firmly upholds the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, unity and political independence of Somalia, and we stress that Somalia’s affairs must be handled by the Somali people themselves. The sanctions should remain targeted, evidence-based and subject to fair and clear procedures, and they must not obstruct humanitarian assistance or undermine the capacity of the Federal Government of Somalia to maintain security. We also stress that all measures related to maritime inspection and information-sharing must be implemented in strict accordance with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and with full respect for the sovereignty and jurisdiction of coastal States and the rights and obligations of flag States. China calls on all regional States to respect Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, refrain from actions that undermine stability, and resolve differences through peaceful dialogue and regional cooperation.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly support the renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, including the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022), and we welcome the focus on arms diversion, maritime trafficking, accountability and conflict-related sexual violence. We stress that AUSSOM must operate with full Somali consent and ownership and receive predictable and sustainable funding, and that all counter-terrorism measures must comply with international humanitarian law and human rights law, including the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace and security.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this resolution. We thank the United Kingdom for its work to maintain Council unity on Somalia. France supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime against Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia, together with the Panel of Experts’ mandate, because these measures are essential to limiting the capacity of terrorist groups that threaten Somalia and the wider region. We welcome the preservation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022), which must be implemented in a way that does not impede principled humanitarian action. France remains particularly concerned by the flow of weapons and ammunition to Al-Shabaab, including from Yemen and by maritime routes, and by reports of links between Al-Shabaab and Houthi actors; the Panel of Experts must be able to investigate these flows and propose additional designations where credible evidence warrants. We also stress the importance of full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity, and of ensuring that AUSSOM operates with the consent and ownership of the Federal Government of Somalia and with predictable funding. The compromise on reviewing the notification and inspection measures applicable to the Federal Government of Somalia, on the basis of progress in arms and ammunition management while maintaining the core embargo on Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia, reflects a balanced approach that France supports. We call on all Member States to implement the sanctions fully and to cooperate with the Committee and the Panel of Experts.
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of this resolution. We welcome the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, together with the strengthened humanitarian safeguards. We underline the importance of respecting Somalia’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and of full compliance with international law, including UNCLOS. Greece also stresses the need to protect maritime security and freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, to strengthen arms and ammunition management to prevent diversion, and to ensure predictable support for AUSSOM, with full respect for Somali ownership.
before.Guyana: Mr. President, Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the United Kingdom for its facilitation and welcome the renewal of the measures and the Panel of Experts’ mandate at a critical moment for Somalia and the region. Guyana supports a targeted sanctions regime that helps degrade Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia while preserving humanitarian access, in line with resolution 2664 (2022). We stress the importance of full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity, including its maritime spaces, and of predictable and sustainable funding for AUSSOM consistent with resolution 2719 (2023). We also underscore the need for robust arms and ammunition management, regional cooperation against illicit weapons flows, protection of civilians, compliance with international humanitarian law, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in peace and security efforts. We support the provisions for review of the sanctions regime and its humanitarian impact, and we will continue to engage constructively to ensure that Council measures support, rather than impede, Somalia’s own counter-terrorism and stabilization efforts.
before.Panama: Panama will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of targeted sanctions against Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia while stressing that humanitarian assistance must not be impeded. We also emphasize the need for full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, and for predictable and sustainable support for AUSSOM, in accordance with international law and the consent of the Federal Government of Somalia.
before.Republic of Korea: Thank you, Mr President. The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts’ mandate as essential tools to counter Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia, while preserving the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664. We also underline the importance of full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, and of predictable support for AUSSOM in close coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia. We call on all Member States to prevent arms diversion and illicit maritime transfers and to ensure that counter-terrorism measures comply with international law and do not impede humanitarian access.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will support the draft resolution. We welcome that our proposal concerning references to cooperation between Al-Shabaab and armed actors in Yemen was taken into account: such references must remain evidence-based and must not prejudge responsibility. We reaffirm that sanctions must be targeted, must not impede humanitarian assistance, and that the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Somalia, as well as Somali ownership of AUSSOM, must be fully respected. We also call for predictable funding for AUSSOM consistent with resolution 2719 (2023) and for the sanctions regime to be reviewed so that it does not undermine the capacity of the Federal Government of Somalia to combat terrorism.
before.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr. President. Sierra Leone votes in favour of this resolution. We welcome the extension of the sanctions measures and the Panel of Experts’ mandate, and we stress that the arms embargo must remain targeted against Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia while fully preserving humanitarian access in accordance with resolution 2664 (2022). We reaffirm the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity of Somalia, and we call for predictable and sustainable financing for AUSSOM consistent with resolution 2719 (2023). Sierra Leone also underscores the importance of protection of civilians, compliance with international humanitarian law, and strengthened cooperation on arms and ammunition management, border security and maritime security. We encourage the Federal Government of Somalia, the African Union and the Panel of Experts to continue their close cooperation, and we remain steadfast in supporting peace and security in Africa.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia votes in favour of this resolution. We support its balanced renewal of targeted sanctions on Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia, while ensuring that humanitarian assistance is not impeded. We also welcome the text’s clear reaffirmation of Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, its focus on international humanitarian law and human rights reporting, and its recognition of the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace and security. We encourage all partners to strengthen arms and ammunition management and to ensure that sanctions remain targeted and effective.
before.Somalia: Mr. President, Somalia takes the floor to express its strong support for the draft resolution before the Council. The text reaffirms Somalia’s sovereignty, political independence, unity and territorial integrity, including over all its land, sea, airspace and maritime territory, and it underscores that all international support, including AUSSOM, must be provided with the full consent and ownership of the Federal Government of Somalia. We welcome the renewal of targeted measures against Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia, the humanitarian safeguards, and the call for predictable and sustainable funding for AUSSOM. We urge all States in the region to respect Somalia’s sovereignty and to refrain from any unilateral arrangements affecting Somali territory without the consent of the Federal Government. Somalia will vote in favour.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks Council members for their constructive engagement on this text. The resolution before us renews targeted measures against Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia, strengthens our collective work against weapons flows from Yemen and maritime trafficking, and preserves humanitarian safeguards through the resolution 2664 exemption. It also reaffirms the sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of Somalia and supports predictable funding for AUSSOM. The United Kingdom will vote in favour and urges the Council to remain united in support of Somalia and in the fight against terrorism.

after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the draft resolution and welcomes its unanimous adoption. We thank the United Kingdom for its efforts to preserve Council unity on this important question.

Pakistan reaffirms its strong support for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Somalia. The threat posed by Al-Shabaab and Islamic State in Somalia remains serious and requires a sustained, coordinated and well-resourced response, including through the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia, operating with the consent and ownership of the Federal Government of Somalia.

We welcome the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts’ mandate, and we stress that these measures must remain targeted, evidence-based and consistent with due process. In particular, the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 must be implemented faithfully so that principled humanitarian assistance is not impeded. We also support strengthened arms and ammunition management to prevent diversion, and call for maritime measures to be implemented in full respect for international law, including UNCLOS, and for the sovereignty and jurisdiction of coastal States.

Pakistan further stresses the need for predictable, adequate and sustainable financing for African Union-led peace support operations, consistent with resolution 2719. We support the central role of the African Union and the principle of African solutions to African problems. Pakistan stands ready to share its counter-terrorism experience and to support capacity-building with Somalia and African partners in the common struggle against terrorism.

Thank you.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President,

Somalia thanks the United Kingdom as penholder and all Council members for the unanimous adoption of this resolution. We welcome the renewal of targeted measures against Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia, the preservation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022), and the attention given to arms and ammunition management, maritime trafficking and predictable funding for AUSSOM.

Somalia voted in favour because this resolution reaffirms the sovereignty, political independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Federal Republic of Somalia, including over all its land, sea, airspace and maritime territory. All international support, including AUSSOM, must continue to be provided with the full consent, ownership and leadership of the Federal Government of Somalia.

We reiterate that sanctions must remain targeted, evidence-based and implemented in a manner that does not undermine the capacity of the Federal Government to defend the country and combat terrorism. We will continue to cooperate fully with the Sanctions Committee and the Panel of Experts, and we call on all partners to support Somali institutions in strengthening accountability, arms and ammunition management, and protection of civilians.

Somalia also calls on all States in the region to respect its sovereignty and territorial integrity and to refrain from any unilateral arrangements affecting Somali territory without the consent of the Federal Government. The Federal Government remains committed to peace, security and stability in Somalia and to working with the Council and all international partners in the fight against terrorism.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. Council unity today sends a clear message of support to Somalia and of determination to degrade Al-Shabaab and IS-Somalia. We are grateful to all Council members for their constructive engagement, which has produced a focused and balanced renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts’ mandate.

The resolution maintains pressure on terrorist groups while preserving the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022), which must be implemented in full so that principled humanitarian action is not impeded. It also strengthens our collective response to arms diversion and illicit maritime trafficking, including weapons flows from Yemen and reported links between Al-Shabaab and Houthi actors. The United Kingdom calls on all Member States to implement the measures fully, including through timely information-sharing and cooperation with the Committee and the Panel of Experts.

We reaffirm our commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity of Somalia. We also underline the importance of predictable and sustainable funding for AUSSOM, consistent with resolution 2719 (2023), and of full Somali ownership and consent. The United Kingdom remains committed to working with Somalia, the African Union, the United Nations and all partners to support peace, security and stability in Somalia and the wider region.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United States voted in favour of this resolution. We thank the United Kingdom for its work as penholder and all Council members for preserving our unity on Somalia.

This renewal is important. Al-Shabaab and ISIS-Somalia continue to threaten Somali civilians, Somali security forces, and regional States. The Panel of Experts remains essential to monitoring implementation of the sanctions measures, documenting diversion, and informing the Committee. We look forward to the swift appointment of the experts so that this work can continue without delay.

The United States remains deeply concerned by the continued flow of weapons and ammunition to terrorist groups in Somalia, including by maritime routes and from Yemen, and by reports of growing links between Al-Shabaab and Houthi actors. We urge all Member States to fully implement the arms embargo, share information on suspicious maritime activity, and take concrete steps to sever the financial and logistical lifelines that sustain these groups.

At the same time, sanctions must remain targeted. We welcome the reaffirmation of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022) and stress that humanitarian assistance must not be impeded by over-compliance or administrative obstacles.

The United States reaffirms its support for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, and unity, and for Somali-led security efforts with AUSSOM and international partners. We will continue to work with the Council to hold terrorist groups accountable and to advance peace and security in Somalia and the wider region. Thank you.
